Alex (SE): Quick check-in for Acme onboarding. We need clear acceptance criteria, a labeled seed set, and answers for their privacy/data flow section by Thu.
Jamie (AE): Acme expects a short trial: demo this week, then a two-week evaluation starting next Monday. They also want an estimated pilot cost today for budget approval.
Maya (CS): They require SSO (SAML) and that evaluation artifacts remain in eu-west-1. Also asked which artifacts we retain post-eval and for how long.
Sam (Security): SSO fine. For regional guarantees: hosted can pin region for storage. If they want complete control over compute residency, Dedicated/Private is necessary. Recommend retention <=14 days for evaluation data unless they sign off.
Ryan (Solutions): For the labeled seed set: propose 120 seeds (80 customer-provided + 40 created by us) covering core intents, edge cases, and failure modes. We'll produce a scoring script and an automated check for regressions.
Leah (PM): Scoring dimensions suggestion: accuracy (0-4), integrity/hallucination (0-3), compliance flags (0/1), and a pass/fail meta column. Add a throughput/latency note as NFR.
Alex (SE): Thresholds I'm proposing: accuracy mean >=3.0, hallucination mean <=0.5, compliance flags <=2% across the sample. p95 latency target < 350ms for hosted.
Jamie (AE): Pricing question: they run ~900 requests/day. Can someone estimate token usage and a rough hosted cost for the trial? Include model recommendation (redwood-moderate-1 or redwood-base-1-q).
Ryan (Solutions): Quick calc: estimate 60 tokens input avg, 180 tokens output avg -> 240 tokens/request -> 216k tokens/day -> 3.02M tokens for 14 days. I'll put a worked example with cost ranges in the repo.
Maya (CS): Who will author the extra 40 prompts and contrived failure cases? We should pair SE + PM for consistent phrasing.
Alex (SE): I'll draft the contrived edge cases. Maya will convert customer examples into standardized prompt templates. Ryan + Leah: we need the CSV schema and an executor script to produce model responses.
Leah (PM): CSV columns: sample_id, prompt_text, gold_reference, response, acc_score, hallucination_score, compliance_flag, annotator, notes. Version via git and keep checkpoints in S3.
Sam (Security): A few security items: S3 must use SSE-KMS, KMS keys per-customer preferred. Need to state we only persist responses for evaluation and purge after agreed retention. Also confirm control plane access is limited to internal admin roles.
Alex (SE): We can commit to SSE-KMS and 14-day retention for this evaluation bucket. We will enable customer-scoped KMS key. Control plane endpoints use mTLS and restricted service accounts.
infra-bot: Environment created: redwood-acme-eval-eu (provisioned by Ryan). Credentials posted to #secure-credentials-perms.
Ryan (Solutions): Recommended harness runbook: 1) put labeled seed CSV at s3://redwood-acme-eval/input/seed_v1.csv 2) run: python run_eval.py --model redwood-moderate-1 --input seed_v1.csv --out s3://redwood-acme-eval/results/v1.csv 3) run: python regression_check.py --baseline s3://redwood-acme-eval/baseline/v1.csv --candidate results/v1.csv
Leah (PM): Regression gates: fail if accuracy drops >4% vs baseline OR hallucination increase >0.25 absolute OR compliance flags increase >1.0%. If marginal, we can schedule a canary rerun.
Alex (SE): For scoring stability, use deterministic decoding for scoring runs (temperature=0, top_p=1). Record RNG seeds and model config in metadata file.
Maya (CS): Acme asked about automated PII redaction before storage. Do we have a supported pipeline?
Sam (Security): Yes, we can run a two-stage redaction: regex heuristics then model-based detector. We'll include redaction logs (what was redacted) but not the redacted content. Need Acme sign-off.
Jamie (AE): Sales note: if they push for Private deployment because of residency or control plane concerns, that will change pricing materially. I'll flag options in the quote.
Leah (PM): Action items: (1) Alex+Maya: finalize the 120-seed set by Wed EOD, (2) Ryan: baseline run + cost breakdown by Wed EOD, (3) Sam: finish privacy/architecture short answers by Thu noon, (4) Leah: publish scoring rubric and gating doc by Thu EOD.
Ryan (Solutions): Baseline path: s3://redwood-acme-eval/baseline/1902/v1.csv. I'll schedule baseline run tonight and upload results.
Alex (SE): One more: Acme prefers deterministic seeds for scoring but wants to see stochastic runs later. We'll do both: deterministic for acceptance, stochastic for behavior analysis.
Maya (CS): I'll collect the 80 examples from Acme and push them to our input bucket. DMing Alex with the raw CSV.
Sam (Security): No major blockers for hosted evaluation as long as SSE-KMS + 14d retention + SSO are accepted. Also confirming we won't enable cross-tenant model fine-tuning without contract.
Jamie (AE): Thanks team. I'll update Acme with the short acceptance checklist: labeled seed pass, latency within target, security answers confirmed, and pilot budget number accepted.
Leah (PM): I'll set the Friday sync with Acme for 11am PT and attach the rubric draft.
Alex (SE): Great. We'll reconvene after baseline uploads. Thanks everyone.
